correctness.rationale: The graph model and domination test are explicit; the strong-regularity neighborhood intersections and inclusion-exclusion prove that no three vertices dominate, while the exhibited four-set does. The 1820 four-subsets and 4368 five-subsets are all enumerated. The jump-edge definition is complete; two independently designed programs reconstruct the graph with different vertex representations, regenerate all feasible subsets and legal swaps, and verify every all-pairs shortest path in the 1056-state five-set graph. Exact multiplicities, symmetry orbits and profiles agree. Full automorphism order 1920 follows from five-generator permutations and a matching stabilizer upper bound. No infinite-family extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: Full text of the 2014 dominating-set reconfiguration paper and the 2020 survey was read at mathematically relevant sections and compared by hypotheses and implications. Their size-cap token addition/removal model and general jump-γ definition do not imply the exact fixed-cardinality five-set exchange graph or its sharp diameter, orbital partition or distance profiles for the Clebsch graph. The existing Clebsch independence complex and perfect-matching/edge-location studies have different configuration objects. Independent-set counts and graph parameters are explicitly prior. Targeted record and primary-literature searches did not uncover covering theorems; possible equivalent unindexed results are an admitted residual risk.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent fixed-five domination-exchange classification may be present in unindexed or inaccessible literature, computational appendices, or data tables.
The Haas–Seyffarth k-Dominating Graph institutional full manuscript was inaccessible during this comparison; its publicly available description covers addition/removal reconfiguration.
The scientific review is internal and does not constitute independent scholarly validation or priority certification.

value.rationale: The classical Clebsch graph is a natural highly symmetric extremal benchmark. Determining the sharp minimal slack needed for reconfiguration is intrinsically motivated by robust vertex placement. The transition from 80 immovable minimum dominating sets to a fully connected one-extra-vertex configuration graph of diameter five is a nontrivial local-to-global structural fact. Five automorphism orbits and exact distance profiles classify all near-optimal states rather than merely recomputing the known graph parameters or an arbitrary slice; the complete finite answer is reusable for domination reconfiguration and algorithms.
